title: CISA SCuBA M365 Secure Configuration Baselines (ScubaGear v2.0.0)
source_citation: CISA Secure Cloud Business Applications (SCuBA) Microsoft 365 baselines, as published with ScubaGear v2.0.0 (released Oct 22, 2026; https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/releases/tag/v2.0.0), CC0 1.0 Universal

items.text: Legacy authentication SHALL be blocked.
Users detected as high risk SHALL be blocked.
A notification SHOULD be sent to the administrator when high-risk users are detected.
Sign-ins detected as high-risk SHALL be blocked. License: Requires a Microsoft Entra ID P2 license
Phishing-resistant MFA SHALL be enforced for all users.
MFA SHALL be enforced for all users.
If Microsoft Authenticator is enabled, it SHALL be configured to show login context information.
The "Authentication methods manage migration" feature SHALL be set to "Migration complete."
The authentication methods of short message service (SMS), voice call, and email one-time passcode (OTP) SHALL be disabled.
Phishing-resistant MFA SHALL be required for highly privileged roles.
Managed devices SHOULD be required for authentication.
Managed devices SHOULD be required to register MFA.
Device code authentication SHOULD be blocked. License: Policies related to managed devices require Microsoft Intune.

Security logs SHALL be sent to the agency's security operations center for monitoring. License: An Azure subscription may be required to send logs to an external system, such as the agency's Security Information and Event Management (SIEM).
Only administrators SHALL be allowed to register applications.
User consent to applications SHALL be restricted.
An administrative consent workflow SHALL be configured for applications.
Application password addition SHOULD be blocked.
Application password lifetime SHOULD be restricted to 180 days or less.
Application certificate lifetime SHOULD be restricted to 365 days or less.
User passwords SHALL NOT expire.
A minimum of two users and a maximum of eight users SHALL be provisioned with the Global Administrator role.
Privileged users SHALL be provisioned with finer-grained roles instead of the Global Administrator role.
Privileged users SHALL be provisioned cloud-only accounts separate from an on-premises directory or other federated identity providers.
Permanent active role assignments SHALL NOT be allowed for highly privileged roles.
Provisioning users to highly privileged roles SHALL NOT occur outside of a PAM system.
Activation of the Global Administrator role SHALL require approval.
Eligible and active highly privileged role assignments SHALL trigger an alert.
User activation of the Global Administrator role SHALL trigger an alert.

User activation of other highly privileged roles SHOULD trigger an alert. License: Policies MS.AAD.7.4v1, MS.AAD.7.5v1, MS.AAD.7.6v1, MS.AAD.7.7v1, MS.AAD.7.8v1, and MS.AAD.7.9v1 require a Microsoft Entra ID P2 license. However, a third-party Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution may also be used to satisfy the requirements. If a third-party solution is used, then a P2 license is not required for the respective policies.
Guest users SHOULD have limited or restricted access to Microsoft Entra ID directory objects.
Only users with the "Guest Inviter" role SHOULD be able to invite guest users.
Guest invites SHOULD only be allowed to be sent to specific external domains that have been authorized by the agency for legitimate business purposes.
Risky AI agents SHALL be blocked. License: Requires a Microsoft Entra ID P2 license and either Microsoft Agent 365 or Microsoft 365 E7.
Automatic forwarding to external domains SHALL be disabled.
An SPF policy SHALL be published for each domain that fails all non-approved senders.
DKIM SHOULD be enabled for all domains.
A DMARC policy SHALL be published for every second-level domain.
The DMARC message rejection option SHALL be p=reject.
The DMARC point of contact for aggregate reports SHALL include `reports@dmarc.cyber.dhs.gov`.
An agency point of contact SHOULD be included for aggregate and failure reports.
SMTP AUTH SHALL be disabled.
Contact folders SHALL NOT be shared with all domains.
Calendar details SHALL NOT be shared with all domains.
External sender warnings SHALL be implemented.
Mailbox auditing SHALL be enabled.
The "Publish to Web" feature SHOULD be disabled unless the agency mission requires the capability.
Guest user access to the Power BI tenant SHOULD be disabled unless the agency mission requires the capability.
The "Invite external users to your organization" feature SHOULD be disabled unless agency mission requires the capability.
Service principals with access to APIs SHOULD be restricted to specific security groups.
Service principals' ability to create and use profiles SHOULD be restricted to specific security groups.
ResourceKey-based authentication SHOULD be blocked unless a specific use case (e.g., streaming and/or "push" datasets) merits its use.
Python and R interactions SHOULD be disabled.

Sensitivity labels SHOULD be enabled for Power BI and employed for sensitive data per enterprise data protection policies. License: A Microsoft Purview Information Protection Premium P1 or Premium P2 license is required to apply or view Microsoft Information Protection sensitivity labels in Power BI. Azure Information Protection can be purchased either standalone or through one of the Microsoft licensing suites. See Microsoft Purview Information Protection service description for details. Microsoft Purview Information Protection sensitivity labels need to be migrated to the Microsoft Information Protection Unified Labeling platform to be used in Power BI. To apply labels to Power BI content and files, a user must have a Power BI Pro or Premium Per User (PPU) license, in addition to one of the previously mentioned Azure Information Protection licenses. Before enabling sensitivity labels on the agency's tenant, ensure sensitivity labels have been defined and published for relevant users and groups. See Create and configure sensitivity labels and their policies for details.
The ability to create production and sandbox environments SHALL be restricted to administrators.
The ability to create trial environments SHALL be restricted to administrators.
A DLP policy SHALL be created to restrict connector access in the default Power Platform environment.
Non-default environments SHOULD have at least one DLP policy.
Power Platform tenant isolation SHALL be enabled.
An inbound/outbound connection allowlist SHOULD be configured.
Content Security Policy (CSP) SHALL be enforced for model-driven and canvas Power Apps.
The ability to create Power Pages sites SHOULD be restricted to administrators.
The "Share with everyone" feature SHOULD be disabled.
Emails with click-to-run file attachments SHALL be blocked including, at a minimum, .exe, .cmd, and .vbe files.
Email scanning SHALL be capable of reviewing emails after delivery.
Emails identified as containing malware SHALL be quarantined or dropped.

SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams message attachments SHOULD be scanned for malware. License: Safe attachments require Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or 2. These are included with E5 and G5 and are available as add-ons for E3 and G3.
User impersonation protection SHOULD be enabled for sensitive accounts.
Domain impersonation protection SHOULD be enabled for domains owned by the agency.
Domain impersonation protection SHOULD be added for key suppliers and partners.

User warnings, comparable to the user safety tips included with EOP, SHOULD be displayed. License: Impersonation protection and advanced phishing thresholds require Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or 2. These are included with E5 and G5 and are available as add-ons for E3 and G3. As of January 2026, anti-phishing for user and domain impersonation and spoof intelligence are not yet available in M365 Government Community Cloud (GCC High) and Department of Defense (DoD) environments. See Platform features | Microsoft Learn for current offerings.

A DLP policy SHALL be configured to protect PII and sensitive information, as defined by the agency, blocking at a minimum: credit card numbers, U.S. Individual Taxpayer Identification Numbers (ITIN), and U.S. Social Security numbers (SSN).
The DLP policy SHOULD be applied to Exchange, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams chat, and Devices.
The action for the DLP policy SHOULD be set to block sharing sensitive information with everyone.
Notifications to inform users and help educate them on the proper use of sensitive information SHOULD be enabled in the DLP policy.

The DLP policy SHOULD include an action to block access to sensitive information by restricted applications License: DLP for Teams requires an E5 or G5 license. See Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention: Data Loss Prevention for Teams | Microsoft Learn for more information. However, this requirement can also be met through a third-party solution. If a third-party solution is used, then an E5 or G5 license is not required for the respective policies. DLP for Endpoint, needed for MS.SECURITYSUITE.3.5v1, requires an E5 or G5 license. See Get started with Endpoint data loss prevention - Microsoft Purview (compliance) | Microsoft Learn for more information. However, this requirement can also be met through a compliant third-party solution. If a third-party solution is used, then an E5 or G5 license is not required for the respective policies.
At a minimum, the following alerts SHALL be enabled:
The alerts SHOULD be sent to a monitored address or incorporated into a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM).
Unified audit logging SHALL be enabled.

Audit logs SHALL be retained and searchable for a minimum of 3 months and retrievable for a minimum of 12 months. License: The creation of a custom audit log retention policy requires E5/G5 licenses or E3/G3 licenses with add-on compliance licenses. To maintain logs in M365 for longer than 180 days, the user generating the logs must have an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license or a Microsoft Purview Suite (formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance) or E5 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license.
Emails detected as spam and phishing SHALL NOT be delivered to the user's inbox.
Allowed domains SHALL NOT be added to inbound anti-spam protection policies.
URL comparison with a block-list SHOULD be enabled for URLs in emails, Teams messages, and Office documents.
Direct download links SHOULD be scanned for malware.
User click tracking SHOULD be enabled. License: Safe links require Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or 2. These are included with E5 and G5 and are available as add-ons for E3 and G3.
IP allow lists SHOULD NOT be created.
Safe lists SHOULD NOT be enabled.
External sharing for SharePoint SHALL be limited to "Existing guests" or "Only people in your organization."
External sharing for OneDrive SHALL be limited to "Existing guests" or "Only people in your organization."
External sharing SHALL be restricted to approved external domains and/or users in approved security groups per interagency collaboration needs.
File and folder default sharing scope SHALL be set to "Specific people (only the people the user specifies)."
File and folder default sharing permissions SHALL be set to view only.
Expiration days for "Anyone" links SHALL be set to 30 days or less.
The allowable file and folder permissions for links SHALL be set to view only.
Reauthentication days for people who use a verification code SHALL be set to 30 days or less.
External meeting participants SHOULD NOT be enabled to request control of shared desktops or windows.
Anonymous users SHALL NOT be enabled to start Microsoft Teams meetings.
Anonymous users and dial-in callers SHOULD NOT be admitted automatically.
Internal users SHOULD be admitted to Microsoft Teams meetings automatically.
Dial-in users SHOULD NOT be enabled to bypass the lobby.
Meeting recording SHOULD be disabled.
"Record an event" SHOULD NOT be set to "Always record."
External access for users SHALL only be enabled on a per-domain basis.
Unmanaged users SHALL NOT be enabled to initiate contact with internal users.
Internal users SHOULD NOT be enabled to initiate contact with unmanaged users.
Microsoft Teams email integration SHALL be disabled.
Agencies SHOULD only allow installation of Microsoft applications approved by the agency.
Agencies SHOULD only allow installation of third-party applications approved by the agency.
Agencies SHOULD only allow installation of custom applications approved by the agency.
